label: What Compy found

door.sub: A game running badly or crashing? Compy can look at what changed on this PC.

firstLook.lead: Compy has no earlier sessions to compare with yet, but it can look at what changed on this PC.
firstLook.leadElsewhere: Pick a game, or the whole PC, and say when it started. Compy will look at what changed on this PC.
firstLook.looking: Looking at what changed on this PC…
firstLook.title: What Compy found on this PC

told.title: What you told Compy
told.today: You said it started today. Compy looked back to {{from}}, in case a change came just before you noticed.
told.thisWeek: You said it started this week. Compy looked back to {{from}}, in case a change came just before you noticed.
told.thisMonth: You said it started this month. Compy looked back to {{from}}, in case a change came just before you noticed.
told.always: You said it has always been like this.
told.dontKnow: You didn't say when it started, so Compy looked at the last 30 days, back to {{from}}.

firstLook.alwaysBody: Changes made recently came after it started, so Compy didn't list them.

group.looksOff: What looks off on this PC
group.looksOffNote: Compy read these on this PC just now. It hasn't measured whether any of them changes how a game runs.

change.gpuInstalled: Windows installed {{adapter}} {{to}} on {{when}}. Compy can't see which version it replaced.
change.gpuInstalledBare: Windows recorded a {{adapter}} install on {{when}}. Compy can't see which version it replaced.
change.otherDrivers_one: Windows installed or updated {{count}} other driver ({{classes}}), the latest on {{when}}.
change.otherDrivers_other: Windows installed or updated {{count}} other drivers ({{classes}}), the latest on {{when}}.
change.programs_one: {{count}} program was installed or updated on {{day}}: {{names}}.
change.programs_other: {{count}} programs were installed or updated on {{day}}: {{names}}.
change.programsMore: {{count}} programs were installed or updated on {{day}}: {{names}} and {{more}} more.
change.updatesMinor: Windows also installed security definition updates ({{n}}) and Store app updates ({{m}}). They are counted here, not listed.
change.updatesUnclassified_one: Windows installed {{count}} update that Compy couldn't classify.
change.updatesUnclassified_other: Windows installed {{count}} updates that Compy couldn't classify.
change.displayOther_one: A display driver ({{count}}) was installed or updated, the latest on {{when}}.
change.displayOther_other: Display drivers ({{count}}) were installed or updated, the latest on {{when}}.
change.gameFiles: Steam changed {{game}}'s files on {{when}}. That can be an update, a file check or added content.
change.gameFilesPending: Steam also shows a newer version of {{game}} that isn't installed yet.
change.modUnknownOn: Compy can't tell whether it is turned on.
change.gameFilesSince: Steam hasn't recorded a change to {{game}}'s files since {{when}}.

how.gpuDriver: To see it: Device Manager, Display adapters, your card, Driver tab. Windows can roll a driver back there if it kept the earlier one.
how.windowsUpdate: To see them: Settings, Windows Update, Update history. Some updates can be uninstalled from that page.
how.programs: To see them: Settings, Apps, Installed apps. Windows keeps one date per program, and some programs refresh it when they update themselves.
how.otherDrivers: To see them: Device Manager shows each device's driver version on its Driver tab.

none.gpuDriver: Windows recorded no graphics driver version change in this period.
none.windowsUpdate: Windows Update recorded no monthly Windows update, Windows version update or driver update in this period.
none.programs: No program shows an install or update date in this period.

firstLook.nothing: Compy found no dated change in this period. That doesn't mean nothing is wrong: Compy hasn't measured how any game runs.
firstLook.unread: Compy couldn't read everything for this period, so it can't say that nothing changed. What it couldn't see is listed below.

limit.title: What Compy couldn't see
limit.classes: Compy reads graphics, audio, network and chipset driver installs only, not other drivers.
limit.noInstallDate: Compy can't see Store apps, or programs that don't record an install date ({{n}} here).
limit.gameNotPicked: Compy didn't look at any game's files, because no game was picked.

why.accessDenied: Windows needs administrator rights to show that log
why.logEmpty: that Windows log is empty or switched off
why.logMissing: this PC has no such Windows log
why.recordsUnreadable: Windows returned {{n}} records Compy couldn't read
why.registry: the list of installed programs couldn't be opened
why.notRead: Compy didn't look it up for this answer
why.tookTooLong: reading took too long, so Compy went on without it
why.partialTimedOut: reading ran out of time, so only the newest records were read
why.partialRowCap: the log holds more records than Compy reads, so older ones are missing
why.partialOutputCapped: the log was too long to read in full
why.partialCoverage: Windows' log only goes back to {{from}}
why.notSteam: this game isn't in a Steam library Compy could read
why.steamUnreadable: Steam's library files couldn't be read
why.steamNoRecord: none of the Steam libraries Compy could read has a record of it
why.steamNoTime: Steam's record has no usable date for when the files changed

limit.steamNewestOnly: Steam keeps only the latest date its files changed for {{game}}, so an earlier change in this period wouldn't show.
limit.hardwareNotReady: Compy is still reading this PC's hardware.
limit.historyUnreadable: Compy couldn't read its own change history.
limit.modsPartialOther: Whether {{game}}'s folder has other graphics mods (only part of the folder was scanned)
limit.modsReaderFailed: Whether {{game}}'s folder has a graphics mod (the reader stopped unexpectedly)
limit.crashesReaderFailed: Whether {{game}} has closed unexpectedly before (the reader stopped unexpectedly)
limit.crashesNoFolder: Whether {{game}} has closed unexpectedly before (Compy couldn't match the game to an install folder)
limit.gameLocation: Compy doesn't know where {{game}} is installed, so it couldn't check its drive or folder.

cantTell.title: What Compy can't tell yet
cantTell.body: Compy hasn't seen a game run yet, so it can't tell whether anything runs worse than before, or which of these changes matters.
cantTell.measure: Compy can measure a game while you play. It needs about 3 sessions of the same game before it can compare. Start a capture in Live, play as usual, and press Check again here afterwards.
cantTell.bodyFew: Compy hasn't got enough sessions of {{game}} yet, so it can't tell whether anything runs worse than before, or which of these changes matters.

firstLook.footer: Compy lists what it can see on this PC. It doesn't say why a game runs badly until it has measured it.

measured.lead: Compy has too few sessions of {{game}} to compare yet ({{have}} of {{need}}).
measured.scope: This list is for the whole PC, not one game.

firstLook.privacy: Compy reads this on your PC. It doesn't save it or send it anywhere, and it doesn't save what you tap.

game.title: Which game?
game.other: Another game, or the whole PC
game.loadingSteam: Looking for your installed Steam games…
game.steamUnread: Compy couldn't read your Steam library.
game.steamPartial: Compy read only part of your Steam library, so some games may be missing.
game.chosenWhole: Looking at the whole PC, not one game.

crash.none: Windows has no crash record for {{game}} in the records Compy read.

split.both_one: Of the crash records Compy could read, at least {{count}} is from before {{date}} (the earliest dated change Compy found) and at least {{after}} from after.
split.both_other: Of the crash records Compy could read, at least {{count}} are from before {{date}} (the earliest dated change Compy found) and at least {{after}} from after.
split.beforeOnly_one: Of the crash records Compy could read, at least {{count}} is from before {{date}} (the earliest dated change Compy found) and none from after.
split.beforeOnly_other: Of the crash records Compy could read, at least {{count}} are from before {{date}} (the earliest dated change Compy found) and none from after.
split.afterOnly: Of the crash records Compy could read, none are from before {{date}} (the earliest dated change Compy found) and at least {{count}} from after. That is a count by date; Compy hasn't tested whether that change matters to the game.
split.beforeUnread_one: Of the crash records Compy could read, at least {{count}} is from before {{date}} (the earliest dated change Compy found). Some records couldn't be read, so it can't say whether any came after.
split.beforeUnread_other: Of the crash records Compy could read, at least {{count}} are from before {{date}} (the earliest dated change Compy found). Some records couldn't be read, so it can't say whether any came after.
split.startsLater_one: Of the crash records Compy could read, at least {{count}} is from after {{date}} (the earliest dated change Compy found). The oldest record it could read is from {{oldest}}, so it can't say how many came before. Windows keeps only a limited number of crash records.
split.startsLater_other: Of the crash records Compy could read, at least {{count}} are from after {{date}} (the earliest dated change Compy found). The oldest record it could read is from {{oldest}}, so it can't say how many came before. Windows keeps only a limited number of crash records.
split.unread_one: Of the crash records Compy could read, at least {{count}} is from after {{date}} (the earliest dated change Compy found). Some records couldn't be read, so it can't say how many came before.
split.unread_other: Of the crash records Compy could read, at least {{count}} are from after {{date}} (the earliest dated change Compy found). Some records couldn't be read, so it can't say how many came before.

running.title: Running right now
running.none: Compy didn't find any program from its list running right now. It matches by program name: recorders and overlays, voice chat, launchers, browsers, build and developer tools, Windows Update.
running.nowGame: This is what is running now, not what was running when the problem with {{game}} happened. Compy didn't see that, and it hasn't measured whether any of these affects a game.
running.nowPc: This is what is running now, not what was running when the problem happened. Compy didn't see that, and it hasn't measured whether any of these affects a game.
running.unread: Compy couldn't read the list of running programs, so it can't say what is running.
running.tookTooLong: Compy didn't finish reading the running programs in time, so it can't say what is running.
running.readerFailed: Compy couldn't read the running programs (the reader stopped unexpectedly).

compy.undone: Compy changed “{{title}}” on {{when}}, and it was undone on {{undone}}.
compy.undoneNoDate: Compy changed “{{title}}” on {{when}}, and it has since been undone.
compy.undoHint: Changes that History lists as applied can be undone there.

fact.monitorRefresh: Your main monitor is running at {{now}} Hz; at this resolution it supports {{max}} Hz.
fact.memorySpeed: Your memory is running at {{now}} MHz; your PC's firmware lists it as capable of {{rated}} MHz.
fact.memoryOneStick: Your PC has 1 memory module, so memory runs in single-channel.
fact.memoryOneChannel: Your {{n}} memory modules all report the same memory channel, so they share one channel.
fact.driveHealth: Windows reports the health of {{drive}} as {{health}}.
fact.gameOnHdd: {{game}} is installed on drive {{drive}}:, which is a hard disk (HDD).
fact.gpuDriverAge_one: Your graphics driver is dated {{date}}, {{count}} day ago.
fact.gpuDriverAge_other: Your graphics driver is dated {{date}}, {{count}} days ago.
fact.freesyncOff: Your AMD graphics card reports FreeSync as off.
fact.onBattery: This PC is running on battery.
fact.gameDriveFull: Drive {{drive}}:, where {{game}} is installed, has {{free}} GB free of {{total}} GB.

factHow.monitorRefresh: To check: Settings, System, Display, Advanced display shows the refresh rate and the ones the monitor supports.
factHow.memorySpeed: To check: Task Manager, Performance, Memory shows the speed it is running at.
factHow.memoryChannels: To check: Task Manager, Performance, Memory shows how many memory slots are used.
factHow.driveHealth: To check: Settings, System, Storage, Advanced storage settings, Disks & volumes shows each drive's health.
factHow.gameOnHdd: To check: Task Manager, Performance, Disk shows whether each drive is an HDD or an SSD.
factHow.gpuDriverAge: To check: Device Manager, Display adapters, your card, Driver tab shows the driver date.
factHow.freesyncOff: To check: AMD Software, Gaming, Display shows the FreeSync setting.
factHow.onBattery: To check: the battery icon in the taskbar shows whether the charger is connected.
factHow.gameDriveFull: To check: Settings, System, Storage shows the free space on each drive.

door.sub: Compy looks at what changed and tells you what it finds.
door.failed: Compy couldn't read its records just now. Nothing on your PC was changed.
door.stillChecking: Compy is still checking. Try again in a moment.

problem.body_one: In a normal session, {{game}}'s dips stay at about {{beforePct}}% of its average frame rate. In your last session they fell to about {{nowPct}}%.
problem.body_other: In a normal session, {{game}}'s dips stay at about {{beforePct}}% of its average frame rate. In your last {{count}} sessions they fell to about {{nowPct}}%.
problem.spikes: The slowest 1 in 100 frames took about {{nowMs}} ms, against about {{beforeMs}} ms in your normal sessions.
problem.average: It also averaged {{nowFps}} frames per second, against about {{beforeFps}} before.
problem.otherGames: {{games}} also had rough sessions in the same period.
problem.partial_one: Compy also saw 1 more session it only measured part of, and what it measured looked rough. A partly measured session never counts on its own.
problem.partial_other: Compy also saw {{count}} more sessions it only measured part of, and what it measured looked rough. A partly measured session never counts on its own.
problem.sinceLasted_one: It last ran normally on {{date}}. The rough run has lasted {{count}} session so far.
problem.sinceLasted_other: It last ran normally on {{date}}. The rough run has lasted {{count}} sessions so far.
problem.earlier: It also ran rough {{from}}–{{to}} and recovered.
problem.sinceLastedFull_one: Its last fully measured normal session was {{date}}. The rough run has lasted {{count}} session so far.
problem.sinceLastedFull_other: Its last fully measured normal session was {{date}}. The rough run has lasted {{count}} sessions so far.
problem.title_one: {{game}} ran much rougher than usual in its last session
problem.title_other: {{game}} has been running much rougher than usual
problem.oneSession: One session isn't much to go on. If the next one is normal, this may have been a one-off.
problem.mixed_one: 1 session ({{dates}}) may contain two games, so Compy didn't judge it.
problem.mixed_other: {{count}} sessions ({{dates}}) may contain two games, so Compy didn't judge them.

answer.mechanism: Often causes this (not measured on your PC)

backgroundLoad.nearby_other: Other programs were seen starting in other recent sessions

memoryPressure.what: Your memory was nearly full while you played

compyChange.what: Compy had a different number of changes on

displayRefreshLower.what: Your screen ran at a lower refresh rate

evidence.driverChanged: Your graphics driver changed from {{from}} to {{to}}.
evidence.sessionsSplit_one: {{game}}'s last normal session ({{date}}) used the old driver; the rough one used the new one.
evidence.sessionsSplit_other: {{game}}'s last normal session ({{date}}) used the old driver; all {{count}} rough ones used the new one.
evidence.crossGame: {{games}} also got much rougher after the update, and never before it.
evidence.installTimeNotRead: Compy didn't read the exact install time; it saw the new version on {{when}}.
evidence.loadNotRecorded: Compy didn't record how busy your PC was in these sessions.
evidence.figureScope: This figure covers everything except the game, including Compy and Windows itself.
evidence.openCounts_one: It was open in {{r}} of {{rm}} rough session and {{n}} of {{nm}} normal ones.
evidence.openCounts_other: It was open in {{r}} of {{rm}} rough sessions and {{n}} of {{nm}} normal ones.
evidence.openCountsNamed_one: {{name}} was open at the start of {{r}} of {{rm}} rough session and {{n}} of {{nm}} normal ones.
evidence.openCountsNamed_other: {{name}} was open at the start of {{r}} of {{rm}} rough sessions and {{n}} of {{nm}} normal ones.
evidence.ramPeak: Memory peaked at {{peakGb}} of {{totalGb}} GB in one rough session.
evidence.ramBaseline: Your normal sessions peaked at {{peakGb}} GB.
evidence.ramWarning: Compy saw memory nearly full during that session.
evidence.ramLower: Other rough sessions only reached {{peakGb}} GB.
evidence.driftApplied: Compy's own check found a setting it applied is no longer on.
evidence.driftPower: Compy noticed the power plan is now one Windows designed to save power.
evidence.driftOther: Compy noticed a setting it watches had changed.
evidence.whichNotRecorded: Which setting it was, and what changed it, isn't recorded.
evidence.countChanged: Compy had {{from}} changes on in the last normal session and {{to}} in the first rough one.
evidence.hardwareChanged: The graphics card or memory Compy recorded is different.
evidence.powerPlanChanged: The power plan recorded on the two sessions is different.
evidence.normalOnNewDriver_one: {{count}} session ran normally on the new driver (on {{date}}).
evidence.normalOnNewDriver_other: {{count}} sessions ran normally on the new driver (the latest on {{date}}).
evidence.partialRoughOnOldDriver: A partly measured session on {{date}}, on the old driver, also looked rough.
evidence.crossGameConfounded: {{games}}'s rough sessions had other programs starting during them, or have no load numbers, so this can't point to the driver alone.
evidence.capChanged: The frame cap went from {{from}} to {{to}}.
evidence.installRecorded: Windows recorded the driver install on {{when}}.
evidence.installNotRecorded: Windows has no record of a graphics driver install in this period, though the driver version Compy saw changed (it saw the new version on {{when}}).
evidence.installAfterRough: Windows recorded a graphics driver install on {{when}}, after the first rough session had started.
evidence.crossGameAfter: {{games}}'s rough sessions also came after the update.
evidence.updateMore_one: {{count}} more update was installed in the same period.
evidence.updateMore_other: {{count}} more updates were installed in the same period.
evidence.filesChanged: Steam says {{game}}'s files changed on {{when}}. That can be an update, a file verification or added content.
evidence.installedAndStarted: {{name}} was installed on {{day}} and also started during the rough sessions.
evidence.otherDriverInstalled_one: Windows recorded {{count}} {{classes}} driver install on {{when}}, and nothing else Compy found lines up with the timing.
evidence.otherDriverInstalled_other: Windows recorded {{count}} {{classes}} driver installs, the first on {{when}}, and nothing else Compy found lines up with the timing.
evidence.reinstallSameVersion: Windows recorded the same driver version being installed again on {{when}}.
evidence.installPriorUnknown: Windows recorded a graphics driver install on {{when}}; the version before it isn't known.
evidence.recoveredSameDriver: {{game}} ran normally again on the same driver ({{version}}). That weakens the driver as the reason, though some driver problems come and go.
evidence.recoveredAfterDriverChange: It recovered after the driver changed to {{version}} on {{when}}.
evidence.recoveredAfterDriverChangeSeen: It recovered after the driver changed to {{version}} (Compy first saw it on {{when}}).
evidence.recoveredQuiet: Compy saw no build or encoding program start, and the rest of your PC was quiet ({{pct}}% CPU used by other programs) in the sessions that ran normally. That is consistent with background programs, but Compy can't see programs that were already running.
evidence.roughLoadNotRecorded: Compy didn't record how busy the PC was in every rough session, so this comparison is one-sided.
evidence.recoveredBusy: Build or encoding programs were still starting, or the rest of your PC was busy, in a session that ran normally. That weakens background programs as the reason.
evidence.recoveredFewStarts: A few build or encoding programs started in the session that ran normally ({{starts}}), so Compy can't say the PC was quiet.
evidence.recoveryLoadNotRecorded: Compy didn't record how busy the PC was in the session that ran normally.
evidence.recoveredRamLower: Memory peaked at {{peakGb}} of {{totalGb}} GB when it ran normally, against {{roughGb}} GB in the rough sessions. That is consistent with memory.
evidence.recoveredRamFull: Memory still peaked at {{peakGb}} of {{totalGb}} GB when it ran normally. That weakens memory as the reason.
evidence.recoveryRamNotRead: Compy has no memory reading for the session that ran normally.
evidence.recoveredDriftStill: Compy's notice about that setting was already there before the session that ran normally, and it still stands. That weakens that setting as the reason.
evidence.recoveryDriftUnknown: Compy can't tell whether that setting was still off when it ran normally.
evidence.recoveredCompySame: Compy had {{count}} changes on when it ran normally, the same as in the rough sessions. That weakens Compy's changes as the reason.
evidence.recoveredCompyBack: Compy's count of changes went from {{from}} to {{to}}, the same number as in the normal sessions before. That is consistent with one of them, but a count can't say which.
evidence.recoveredCompyOther: Compy's changes went from {{from}} to {{to}} between the rough sessions and the one that ran normally.
evidence.recoveryCompyUnread: Compy has no change count for one of those sessions.
evidence.recoveredBuildSame: Windows was still build {{build}} when it ran normally. That weakens that update as the reason.
evidence.recoveredBuildChanged: Windows changed from build {{from}} to {{to}} between the rough sessions and the one that ran normally.
evidence.recoveryBuildUnread: Compy has no Windows build for one of those sessions.
evidence.recoveredUnchangedUpdate: Windows recorded no further update between the rough sessions and the one that ran normally, so the update was most likely still in place. That weakens it as the reason.
evidence.recoveredUnchangedFiles: Steam recorded no further change to {{game}}'s files between the rough sessions and the one that ran normally, so the files were most likely the same. That weakens them as the reason.
evidence.recoveredUnchangedProgram: Windows recorded no further program install between the rough sessions and the one that ran normally, so the program was most likely still there. That weakens it as the reason.
evidence.recoveredChangedAgainUpdate: Windows recorded another update on {{when}}, between the rough sessions and the one that ran normally.
evidence.recoveredChangedAgainFiles: {{game}}'s files changed on {{when}}, and it has run normally in the sessions since.
evidence.recoveredChangedAgainProgram: Windows recorded another program install on {{when}}, between the rough sessions and the one that ran normally.
evidence.recoveryRecordsUnread: Compy couldn't read Windows' records for the time since, so it can't say whether this changed again.
evidence.recoveredDriverRecordDiffers: Windows recorded a graphics driver install on {{when}} that the sessions' driver version doesn't show, so Compy can't say.
evidence.recoveryDriverUnread: Compy has no driver version for one of those sessions.
evidence.compyChangesDiffer: Compy's count of changes that are on also changed, from {{from}} to {{to}}, between the rough sessions and the one that ran normally.
evidence.startsSeen_one: {{count}} rough {{game}} session had other programs starting during it ({{names}}).
evidence.startsSeen_other: {{count}} rough {{game}} sessions had other programs starting during them ({{names}}).
evidence.startsSeenNoNames_one: {{count}} rough {{game}} session had other programs starting during it.
evidence.startsSeenNoNames_other: {{count}} rough {{game}} sessions had other programs starting during them.

evidence.recoveredSteamLatestOnly: Steam only keeps the latest update time of {{game}}'s files, and that is after the rough sessions, so Compy can't say whether they changed in between.
evidence.modFilesCreated: Files of this mod were created in this folder around {{first_seen}} (Windows resets this date when a folder is copied or moved, so it is not necessarily when the mod was added).
evidence.modSettingsChanged: Its settings file was last changed on {{date}}.
evidence.modLogWritten: The mod's own log or cache file was last written on {{date}}.
evidence.modLogBeforeRough: That is before the rough session.
evidence.crossGameMod: {{otherGame}}'s folder contains {{name}} files, so its rough sessions may have their own reason.
evidence.crossGameModUnchecked: Compy couldn't check {{otherGame}}'s folder for graphics mods.

fix.title: How to fix it

gpuDriver.step1: Press Windows + X and open Device Manager.
gpuDriver.step2: Open Display adapters, double-click your graphics card, then open the Driver tab.
gpuDriver.step3: If "Roll Back Driver" can be clicked, click it and restart. Your previous version was {{from}}.
gpuDriver.step4: If it's greyed out, download {{from}} from the graphics maker's previous-drivers page, run it, and choose the clean install option.
gpuDriver.step5: Then play {{game}} once and press Something's wrong again. Compy will compare it with how it usually runs.

backgroundLoad.step1NoNames: Close other programs, especially anything building, recording or downloading, while you play.
backgroundLoad.step2: Play {{game}} once with them closed, then press Something's wrong again.
backgroundLoad.stepProgram: Close {{name}} before you play, then play once and press Something's wrong again.

memoryPressure.step1: Close browser tabs and launchers before you play. Memory peaked at {{peakGb}} of {{totalGb}} GB.
memoryPressure.step2: Play {{game}} once, then press Something's wrong again.

settingDrift.step1: Open History to see what Compy changed, and check any Windows setting you changed yourself.
settingDrift.step2: Play {{game}} once, then press Something's wrong again.

compyChange.step1: Open History and look at the changes Compy has on. Undo the newest one.
compyChange.step2: Play {{game}} once, then press Something's wrong again.

fix.none: There's nothing safe Compy can change for this. Check it in Windows, then play once more.

frameCapChange.step1: Set the frame cap in the game or in your graphics settings back to what it was ({{from}}), or leave it as it is.
frameCapChange.step2: Play {{game}} a few times. Compy only compares like with like, and needs 3 normal sessions with the new setting.

windowsUpdate.step1: Open Settings, then Windows Update, then Update history to see what was installed and when.
windowsUpdate.stepUninstall: If you want to test it, Update history has "Uninstall updates". You can remove {{kb}} there and restart. That's your choice; Compy won't do it for you.
windowsUpdate.step2: Play {{game}} once, then press Something's wrong again.

gameFiles.step1: Check {{game}}'s patch notes for what changed around that date.
gameFiles.step2: In Steam, right-click {{game}}, open Properties, then Installed Files, and choose Verify integrity of game files.
gameFiles.step3: Play {{game}} once, then press Something's wrong again.

programInstalled.step1: Close {{names}} while you play, or uninstall it if you don't need it.
programInstalled.step2: Play {{game}} once, then press Something's wrong again.

graphicsMod.step1: Check {{name}}'s own page for a newer version.
graphicsMod.step2: To test without it, move its files out of the game folder (or use its own uninstall), play once, and press Something's wrong again.

gpuHotter.step1: Check that the card's fans spin up when you play, and look at the fans and heatsink for dust.
gpuHotter.step2: Check that the case has clear airflow in and out, and look at the card's fan curve in its own tool (it may be set too low).
gpuHotter.step3: Play {{game}} once, then press Something's wrong again.

card.notProven: Compy can't prove this until you try the fix and play again.
card.scrollLabel: What Compy found. Scrolls if there is more.
card.somethingElse: Something else? Answer a few questions

why.crossGame: It changed just before {{game}} got rough, and {{games}} got rough right after it too. The other changes don't line up with every rough session.
why.tie: Two changes line up equally. Start with the one that's easier to undo.
why.crossGameLead: It changed just before {{game}} got rough, and {{games}} got rough right after it too.

nothingWrong.title: Nothing looks wrong
nothingWrong.body_one: {{game}}'s last session ran the way it usually does. If something still feels off, tell Compy what you notice and play once more with Compy running.
nothingWrong.body_other: {{game}}'s last {{count}} sessions ran the way it usually does. If something still feels off, tell Compy what you notice and play once more with Compy running.

cantTell.title: Compy can't tell yet
cantTell.needsMore: Compy needs {{total}} normal sessions of {{game}} to know what normal is. You have {{have}}.
cantTell.partial: Compy only measured part of your last {{game}} session ({{percent}}%), so it won't judge it. Play once more with Compy running.
cantTell.crash: Crashes have their own page for now. Open Problems to see what Windows recorded.
cantTell.noGame: Compy hasn't recorded {{game}} yet. Compy can measure a game while you play. It needs about 3 sessions of the same game before it can compare. Start a capture in Live, play as usual, and press Check again here afterwards.
cantTell.noSessions: Compy hasn't recorded any games yet. Compy can measure a game while you play. It needs about 3 sessions of the same game before it can compare. Start a capture in Live, play as usual, and press Check again here afterwards.
cantTell.partialRough: Compy only measured part of your last {{game}} session ({{percent}}%), and what it saw looked rough. Play once more with Compy running.
cantTell.frameCap: Your frame cap changed, or Compy can't read it, between your earlier {{game}} sessions and the newest one, so it won't compare them.
cantTell.backToNormal: Compy can't tell yet whether {{game}} is back to normal. Play once more.
cantTell.oneClear: One session since has run the way {{game}} usually does. Compy needs one more to be sure.
cantTell.recoveryCap: {{game}}'s frame cap is different now, so Compy can't compare these sessions with the earlier ones.

nothingChanged.title: Compy measured the problem, but nothing it records changed before it
nothingChanged.next: Play once more and Compy will compare again.

footer: Compy lists what changed before the problem. It doesn't claim to know the cause until a fix is checked.

notSeparable.title: Compy can't tell which of these it is yet

notSeparable.nextOther: Play {{game}} once more. Compy may still not be able to tell these apart.
